extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners learning arithmetic/algebra (historic Italian treatise)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, procedures and explanatory principles for multiplying, adding, and manipulating quantities (including multi-term polynomials and figurate numbers) as presented in a historical Italian arithmetic/algebra treatise. Covers unit/denomination conversion, cross/grid multiplication, binomial/trinomial products, and carrying/reduction conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of multiple multiplication methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Different legitimate ways of multiplying a quantity (multiplying by parts, by hundreds, by numbers, etc.) should produce the same final product; performing the same multiplication by two or more valid methods must yield equivalent results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly emphasizes that one may 'multiplicare e partire' by many modes (es.: partire per cento per cento, per numero, per centinaia, partendo per cento per cento ecc.) and that if done correctly the various methods produce the same quantity ("piu via piu fa piu, via meno fa meno"; "piu via piu fa piu, ne piu ne meno"). If different results appear, the method must be checked. The author also notes practical ways (crosses/cells) to ensure completeness of the work so as to avoid omissions or extra entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of a core set of multiplication rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite, explicit set of fundamental multiplication rules is sufficient to generate all other practical modes of multiplication encountered in arithmetic and algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise states that the enumerated rules ('quelle regole quali in substanzia') provide sufficiency: 'le regole sono alla sufficientia e li modi possono accadere... i altri modi non è immaginabile potere occorrere' — i.e., from the basic rules one can derive the other modes. The implication is to learn and rely on these core rules rather than invent ad hoc methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert to common denomination when combining quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantities having different denominations or units must be converted to a common denomination (or expressed with equivalent units) before performing addition or certain multiplications; denominations that are not mutually reducible require care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text discusses that quantities in algebra have various 'unità' and 'denominazioni' and that you cannot add unlike denominations without conversion ('le quantità ... le unità son varie e diverse ... non si possono ridure'). Practical examples and discussion appear throughout: to sum terms you often must transform them to a common denomination or bring them into comparable units before summing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete the cross/cell (crocetta/cafella) when multiplying polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiplying multi-term expressions (binomials, trinomials, etc.), one must construct and completely fill the multiplication cross/grid (the 'crocetta' or 'cafella') — neither omitting entries nor adding extraneous ones — to obtain the correct total product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author instructs explicitly: 'finire tutta la crocetta ouer cafella... non più né meno' and warns against doing too much or too little in the grid. There are examples where the product is obtained by completing every cell of the cross and summing the partials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figurate correspondence for binomials/trinomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Binomials, trinomials, quadrinomials correspond to 2-, 3-, 4-figures respectively; their multiplication follows rules that produce the appropriate number of figurate components (e.g., two figures produce four via combinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text states 'le binomi vanno còrno Doi figure... i trinomi còrno le 3 figure... nel trattato de la multiplicatione j' insegnerai per doi figure...' and gives counts (e.g., 'per doi figure... per 24 via...') — instructing that algebraic multi-term multiplication can be seen and organized in terms of figurate combinations. This guides how to arrange and enumerate partial products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure properties: product of squares (and cubes) retains shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Products of square numbers produce a square (under the given constructions/representations); similarly, products of cubes produce a cube in the described sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages state: 'tutti sono quadrati... il prodotto... quadrato' and analogously for cubes: 'dei numeri cubo... il cubo se multiplica... il prodotto cubico' — the treatise uses geometric/figurative language to assert that squares and cubes multiply to give figures of the same genus when combined by the described methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for carrying ('abattuto') and denomination dominance
rubrics_metrics.description: When sums or partial products exceed a denomination, carry (abattuto) to the next higher denomination and follow the dominance of the greatest denomination ('magior Denominatione') when arranging and reducing terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author discusses how larger denominations govern carrying and reduction: 'la magior Denominatione... fra quelle due quantità più ... la magior Denominatione intendiamo quella che otto maggior numero ci fa presentate' and gives examples of carrying/abattuto ('abattuto fa più... Debito gionto a Debito fa più'). Practical instructions show how to handle overflows between columns/denominations when summing or organizing the partials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group and reduce equal denominations to simplify computation
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple quantities share the same denomination, group them (sum their counts) and reduce to simpler terms or to higher denomination units where appropriate to simplify the computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text instructs grouping: 'se molte quantità sono di una denominazione... si possono raggruppare e ridurre' and provides procedures for adding like-denominated terms, combining multiplicities, and reducing to more convenient denominations for further operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiply by parts and sum partial products
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommended method is to multiply by parts: decompose one factor into parts, multiply each part by the other factor, and then sum the partial products to get the final result (the usual distributive approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise gives many directives using 'partire' and 'partendo' ('partire per cento per cento', 'partendo per numero') and shows that one may start with convenient parts (hundreds, tens, etc.), multiply each and then 'compendierà summa.' This is illustrated with examples and the admonition to line up and add the partial products correctly (tie-in with crocetta/cafella).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer memorization of frequent rules and clear notation
rubrics_metrics.description: For efficient practice, memorize the frequently occurring rules and adopt concise notations or symbols for recurrent operations to reduce error and speed computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author recommends that certain frequently used rules be committed to memory ('la verità di queste regole ... facilmente a memoria') and suggests conventions and notations (marks/segni) to make repeated operations less error-prone. He also points out which forms are most common and therefore worth internalizing.
